clue.text: Out of date cotton fabrics for maids

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it, so one piece leaves the longer word

parts.note: aida is an open-weave cotton cloth used for cross-stitch
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned cotton cloth is being issued to the household maids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of date' reads as one phrase meaning old-fashioned, but it splits: 'Out of' removes, and 'date' is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An aia (ayah) is an Indian nursemaid or lady's maid, a word from the days of the Raj.

clue.text: Light field gun in a US carrier

parts.note: taken as written
a musette bag is the small knapsack carried by US soldiers

explanation.surface: A lightweight field gun is shipped aboard an American aircraft carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrier' points to a warship; it is a bag. A musette is also a small bagpipe, which may help recall the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusette was an 18th-century light field gun, a sort of oversized musket fired from a stand.

clue.text: Indian retreats from stuff in a quiet square

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written
sh is a call for quiet
to ram is to stuff or cram
S for square

explanation.surface: Indian hermitages are built from materials gathered in a peaceful town square.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious hermitage or community where people retreat for meditation.

clue.text: Son combined with mother

parts.note: S for son
cum is Latin for with, used to join two things, as in a kitchen-cum-diner

explanation.surface: A son and his mother joined together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' wants to be the parent; it is the slimy film that forms on fermenting liquids.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother is the scummy film of bacteria that forms on vinegar or wine, so scum is a fair synonym.

clue.text: With reference to Heartbeat, shooting is costly

indicators.note: shooting suggests letters flying off in all directions and landing in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Filming the TV police drama Heartbeat on location turns out to be expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartbeat was a long-running British TV police drama set in 1960s Yorkshire; the capital H disguises the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Systole is the contraction phase of the heart's pumping cycle, so systolic is the adjective relating to it.

clue.text: Certain very fast burglary

parts.note: a safe bet is a certain one
a cracking pace is a very fast one

explanation.surface: A particular burglary was carried out at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certain' reads as 'a particular' in the surface but means sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Safecracking is breaking into safes to steal their contents, a specialist kind of theft by breaking in.

clue.text: Fixed in one of their camps, four from Rome secured by public

definitions.text: Fixed in one of their camps

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast within it

parts.note: public as in state-owned, state schools
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four Roman soldiers are held by the public in one of their own camps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' refers back to the Romans of the clue, which is why the definition reaches past the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman stative camp was a permanent, stationary one, as opposed to a marching camp; stative means fixed.

clue.text: Consider endlessly lively dances items difficult to remember

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to consider is to think
gamy, spirited and plucky
jigs are lively folk dances

explanation.surface: Keep pondering those energetic dances whose names you can't recall.
explanation.definitionFit: Thingamyjigs are what you call objects whose proper name escapes you, placeholders for forgotten words.

clue.text: Yearn for start of tiffin with unfashionable black tea

indicators.note: one word for another means it stands in that place, replacing it

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: opening letter of tiffin
to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: Pining for the first course of an old-fashioned tiffin with black tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiffin is a light lunch or afternoon snack in Anglo-Indian usage. 'For' here means 'in place of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oulong is a variant spelling of oolong, a partly fermented Chinese tea, here classed as black tea.

clue.text: Inferior fleeting shows lacking attendant troops

parts.note: INF is the abbreviation for inferior

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so those letters go

parts.note: pageantry is empty show or display
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: Second-rate passing spectacles that have no ushers among the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers, and the plural infantries means several bodies of such troops.

clue.text: Crack in Glasgow left out? Buy up there

indicators.note: with something out, it has been taken away and is no longer present

parts.note: cloff is a Scots word for a cleft or fissure
L for left

explanation.surface: Is a crack in Glasgow being left out? Go and buy one up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up there' means in Scotland, matching 'in Glasgow': both the wordplay word and the answer are Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Coff is an old Scots verb meaning to buy, so a purchase made north of the border.

clue.text: China must start to suspect phoney local grass

indicators.note: something phoney is fake, so the letters before it are not genuine in their order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of suspect

explanation.surface: Beijing ought to start suspecting a phoney grass, an informer, in its own district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' in the surface hints at an informer; here it is the plant. 'Local' ties it to the China of the clue, where the grass grows wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscanthus is a tall ornamental grass native to East Asia, including China, also grown as a biofuel crop.

clue.text: Parking road rage I fancy triggers summoning device

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters get dressed up in a new order

parts.note: P for parking, as on road signs
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parking dispute that I imagine sparks road rage sets off an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiopager is a pocket bleeper that alerts the wearer to call in, used to summon doctors on call.

clue.text: Court official has trouble stopping strike

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to biff is to hit or punch
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A court official runs into difficulty when trying to halt an industrial strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like a walkout to be stopped; it is a blow, and the trouble goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is an officer of the court who serves writs and enforces its orders, such as seizing goods.

clue.text: Twig section soldiers surrounded by artillery

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for section

indicators.note: whatever is surrounded by something sits inside it, enclosed on all sides

parts.note: ART is a standard abbreviation for artillery
soldiers as the rank and file, the men

explanation.surface: A section of soldiers is hemmed in by enemy artillery fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarment is a slender runner or twig, especially a vine shoot; a rare botanical word.

clue.text: King John not against cracking on

indicators.note: something cracking another breaks into it, so it ends up lodged inside

parts.note: of and on are interchangeable in phrases like a book of, or on, birds

indicators.note: not here tells us to drop the word that follows from what precedes it

parts.note: a john is a lavatory, informally a lav
V for versus, against

explanation.surface: King John is not opposed to cracking on with things.
explanation.walkthrough: King John reads as the English monarch; 'King' is the definition alone and 'John' is the toilet. Olaf is a recurring name among Norwegian kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings of Norway and Denmark were called Olaf, St Olaf being the best known, so the name stands for a king.

clue.text: Dutch product reckoned to be from the east

indicators.note: across clues normally read west to east, so reading from the east runs the word backwards

parts.note: made as in made it to be ten, worked out or reckoned

explanation.surface: A Dutch export was thought to have come originally from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is the round red-waxed cheese named after the town in the Netherlands where it originated.

clue.text: Good number in Chinese society showing hair rolls

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: CHIN is a dictionary abbreviation for Chinese
G for good
NO is the abbreviation for number
S for society

explanation.surface: Plenty of Chinese society ladies wear their hair coiled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good number' reads as a large quantity; it is two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A chignon is a knot or coil of hair worn at the back of the head, so plural for several such rolls.

clue.text: Old rarely spotted rickety sled on view for audience

indicators.note: something rickety is falling apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard by listeners, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: a view is a scene

explanation.surface: A rarely seen, rickety old sled is put on show for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the definition as archaic; 'on' in a down clue places one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Seld-seen is an archaic compound meaning seldom seen, seld being the old form of seldom.

clue.text: Pole put back retracted kitchen counters, for example

indicators.note: something retracted is drawn back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: S for the South Pole
to remit is to postpone or put back to a later date

explanation.surface: A Pole renovating a kitchen pushes back the worktops he had pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counters' suggests worktops in the surface; in the definition they are devices that count down minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen timers count down cooking minutes, so they are literally counters found in a kitchen.

clue.text: Revolutionary lines up assassin as before

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, the reverse direction

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
rows are lines

explanation.surface: A rebel lines up the hitman, just as he did last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an obsolete sense; Shakespeare uses the word for a cut-throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworder in old usage is a gladiator or cut-throat, one who kills with a sword, hence an assassin.

clue.text: Naval officer Jack's on the Beeb

parts.note: J for jack in a card pack
Auntie and the Beeb are both nicknames for the BBC

explanation.surface: A naval officer called Jack appears on BBC television.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack suggests a sailor, fitting the naval surface; it is only the card abbreviation. 'On' in a down clue places one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Jauntie is a variant of jaunty, naval slang for the master-at-arms, the ship's chief disciplinary officer.

clue.text: Medical officer sharing military awards in form of crosses

indicators.note: sharing space with others means sitting among them, inside the group

parts.note: the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration
MO is the abbreviation for medical officer

explanation.surface: A medical officer shares military medals, all in the shape of crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' suggests the shape of medals such as the Military Cross; it means hybrid animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A dsomo is a dzo, a cross between a yak and a domestic cow kept in the Himalayas, so a hybrid.

clue.text: Talk over nobleman engaging Mike Pence

indicators.note: to engage someone is to take them in, so the nobleman holds the other letters within

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
Mike is the radio code word for M
P is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: Discuss a British aristocrat hiring US Vice-President Mike Pence.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Pence looks like the American politician, but it splits into a radio code word and money.
explanation.definitionFit: Emparl is an obsolete form of parley, meaning to confer or hold discussions with someone.

clue.text: Letters half erased on transcript for old survey

indicators.note: half of the word is rubbed out, so only its front portion remains

parts.note: epistles are letters, as in the New Testament
a transcript is a written copy

explanation.surface: Some letters were partly rubbed out on a transcript of an old survey.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopy is an obsolete word for oversight or supervision, from the Greek for overseeing, so an old word for a survey.

clue.text: Recall detectives arresting proper pig

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read back to front
arresting someone means holding them, so the outer word grips the inner one

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
U means upper-class, hence socially proper or acceptable

explanation.surface: Call back the detectives who are arresting a genuine pig, slang for a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: U as upper-class or proper is a crossword convention from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A suid is any member of the Suidae, the zoological family of pigs and hogs.

clue.text: Leader of criminals on an Italian river?

definitions.text: Leader of criminals on an Italian river?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its head, so just that one is taken

parts.note: opening letter of criminals
an is the indefinite article, A
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss is spotted somewhere along the banks of an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a playful description, a Mafia boss found beside an Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A capo is a high-ranking member of a Mafia family, the head of a crew of criminals in Italian slang.

clue.text: Chinese pillory corporal punishment in parts

indicators.note: parts as a verb means departs or leaves, so the word before it goes

parts.note: caning, beating with a cane
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Chinese pillory was used partly as a form of physical punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In parts' reads as 'partly'; split it, and 'in' is the thing that departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cang, or cangue, was a heavy wooden collar locked round an offender's neck in imperial China.

clue.text: Lances concerning Carmen?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Carmen Jones is Hammerstein's musical reworking of Bizet's Carmen

explanation.walkthrough: Carmen suggests Bizet's bullfighting opera, which fits the lances; here she supplies the surname from Carmen Jones, the musical version.
explanation.definitionFit: Rejones are the wooden lances used by a mounted bullfighter, the rejoneador, to wound the bull.

clue.text: Leaving Belgium, there's extra payment as duty

indicators.note: when something is leaving it goes away, so it is taken from the word

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: When you leave Belgium you pay extra as customs duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' suggests a tax in the surface but means obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, so it is a duty one is obliged to carry out.

clue.text: Supports detaining school reptiles

indicators.note: detaining someone keeps them held within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: aids are supports or helps
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: Staff who support pupils keep some reptiles in school as class pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests a place of learning, but it is a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamids are lizards of the family Agamidae, which includes the bearded dragon and frilled lizard.

clue.text: A crazy guy in concealed spot gets the bird

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a hide is a concealed shelter for watching wildlife
a and one both mean a single item

indicators.note: crazy means disordered, so the letters it describes are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A madman lurking in a hidden place is given the bird, jeered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' is an idiom for being booed, but 'the bird' alone is the definition. A hide is the birdwatcher's hut, which suits the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The honeyguide is an African bird known for leading people and badgers to bees' nests to share the honey.

clue.text: Charm's shown repeatedly by Queen protected by soldiers

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the same assembled chunk is written out more than once in a row
something protected by another is shielded within it, so it goes inside

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
R for Regina, queen
the same soldiers again, as the clue asks for a repeat
the same queen again, inside the second set

explanation.surface: A queen's charm is displayed again and again under military guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen inside the soldiers makes one half, and 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gris-gris is an amulet or talisman from West African and voodoo tradition, believed to ward off evil.

clue.text: Darned report switching sides

indicators.note: sides here are compass points, and switching them swaps the north and south letters

parts.note: news is a report of events

explanation.surface: A damning report has a politician changing parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darned' looks like a mild curse; it is the past participle of darn, to mend.
explanation.definitionFit: To darn a sock is to mend it with needle and thread, so a darned hole has been stitched up.
